texts.common.the_8_kb_boot_rom_inside_the: The 8 KB boot ROM inside the Disk System's RAM adapter. A Famicom disk cannot start without it. The 'FDS BIOS to Use' setting chooses which dump. A cartridge needs none.
texts.error.fds_needs_bios: This is a Famicom Disk System disk image, which needs the 8192-byte Disk System BIOS. Choose it on the firmware page.
texts.error.fds_no_side: The disk has no such side.
texts.error.fds_save_header: The Disk System save data has a header this core cannot read.
texts.error.fds_save_sides: The Disk System save data has a different number of disk sides from the disk.
texts.error.fds_save_truncated: The Disk System save data ends early.
texts.error.fds_short: The disk image is a side short.
texts.error.fds_side_truncated: A side of the disk image ends early.
texts.error.fds_size: The disk's size is not the one it declares.
texts.error.fds_too_small: The disk is too small for what it holds.
texts.error.no_file: No game file is in the project.
texts.error.no_prg: The iNES header declares no PRG ROM.
texts.error.no_saves: This machine keeps no saves (it has no battery and no disk), so '%1' would not be read.
texts.error.not_ines: The file is not an iNES file.
texts.error.save_size: The save file is the wrong size for this cartridge.
texts.error.smaller_than_header: The file is smaller than an iNES header.
texts.error.too_small: The file is smaller than the sizes its header declares.
texts.error.trainer: A file with a trainer is not supported.
texts.error.unsupported_mapper: The cartridge's mapper is not supported. This core has NROM, SxROM, UxROM, CNROM, TxROM, AxROM, GxROM and mapper 70.
texts.firmware.bios.label: Nintendo FDS
texts.setting.allowmorethaneightsprites.about: Draws every sprite on a line instead of the eight the real console can show, which removes flicker. BizHawk treats this as a display option. It can change a timing signal some games rely on (the sprite-zero hit), though, so here it is part of the machine and changing it restarts the core.
texts.setting.apuvolume.about: The volume of the sound chip, from 1 to 10. It is the same as NesHawk's APU volume slider.
texts.setting.backgroundcolor.about: The colour used for pixels the video chip never drew, as 0xRRGGBB written as a decimal number. -1 leaves them in the palette's own background colour, as NesHawk does by default.
texts.setting.clipleftandright.about: Blanks the 8 leftmost and 8 rightmost columns of the picture. Real televisions cut them off, and many games leave garbage there. BizHawk makes the picture narrower. Here the picture keeps its size and the columns are black.
texts.setting.dispbackground.about: Draws the background layer. It changes the picture only. The video chip still processes the layer, so the game's timing is not affected.
texts.setting.dispsprites.about: Draws the sprite layer. It changes the picture only, like Display Background.
texts.setting.fdsbios.about: Which Disk System BIOS the machine starts with. It is shown only for a Famicom Disk System project, and it decides which firmware file the wizard's firmware page asks for.
texts.setting.initialwramstatepattern.about: The bytes the console's 2 KB of main memory hold at power-on, written in hex (for example 'FF' or 'DE AD BE EF'). Empty means the pattern FCEUX uses, which is also NesHawk's default. A few games (Cybernoid, Huang Di) behave differently with another pattern.
texts.setting.machine.about: Which machine this project is: a cartridge console, or a console with the Famicom Disk System attached. The wizard asks this first because everything after it depends on the answer. A cartridge project takes a .nes file and needs no firmware. A Disk System project takes a .fds file and starts through the Disk System's BIOS. The choice is saved in the project and recorded in the movie, and is never guessed from a file name.
texts.setting.ntscbottomline.about: The last picture line shown on an NTSC machine.
texts.setting.ntsctopline.about: The first picture line shown on an NTSC machine. NesHawk crops the picture. Here the picture keeps its size and the lines outside are black.
texts.setting.palbottomline.about: The last picture line shown on a PAL or Dendy machine.
texts.setting.palette.about: Which of NesHawk's colour palettes the picture uses. 'quickNES' is the default. '2c03' and '2c04' are the palettes of the arcade versions of the video chip.
texts.setting.paltopline.about: The first picture line shown on a PAL or Dendy machine.
texts.setting.port1.about: What is plugged into controller port 1. Only the standard controller is supported so far. NesHawk also offers light guns, Arkanoid paddles and the Four Score adapter.
texts.setting.port2.about: What is plugged into controller port 2. An empty port always reads as 0, which a game can tell apart from a connected controller. Some games and glitches depend on it.
texts.setting.region.about: Which regional model this is. It changes the frame rate, the processor speed and the number of lines the video chip draws, so changing it restarts the core. BizHawk's 'Default' looks the region up in its cartridge database. This core has no such database and starts as NTSC.
texts.slot.rom.help: The game. It is either a cartridge file in iNES format (.nes) or a Famicom Disk System image (.fds). A disk needs the FDS BIOS, which the next wizard page asks for. A cartridge needs none.
texts.slot.savedata.help: The saved game the machine starts with. This is the file that Emulator > Export Save Data... writes. It is battery.sav for a cartridge with a battery, and disk.sav for a Famicom Disk System, where the save is the difference between the disk as it is now and the disk that was loaded. The file is never changed. The project and the movie record exactly which file it was, so a movie that starts from a saved game can be played back by anyone who has the same file. A machine that keeps no saves (no battery and no disk) says so.
